header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, CIRCUIT COURT, MIRPURKHAS
(Asad Ali and another vs. The State)
Applicants : 1. Asad Ali son of Meedan @ Muhammad Hussain,
Through Mr. Altaf Hussain Junejo, Advocate.
body: NISAR AHMED BHANBHRO, J: Through the instant bail application, applicants Asad Ali son of Meedan @ Muhammad Hussain and Mst. Waseeman wd/o Sajjad Ali seek post-arrest bail under Section 497 Cr.P.C in F.I.R bearing Crime No.58 of 2026, registered at police station Taluka Tando Adam for offences punishable under Sections 324, 336, 504, 34 PPC. Their earlier application for post arrest bail was dismissed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II, Tando Adam vide order dated 09.09.2026.

2. The prosecution case in nutshell is that on 21.06.2026 scuffle between Sajjad Ali, Asad and Mst. Waseeman wife of Sajjad took place in the house. Thereafter, it is alleged that accused Asad took bottle of petrol from his pocket and spilt it over Sajjad. Thereafter, Mst. Waseeman burnt the stick of match, set him on fire and went away. The complainant party moved Sajjad Ali to the hospital at Shahdadpur. Thereafter, he was shifted to Hyderabad, where he succumbed to his injuries during treatment. The complainant lodged the FIR on 24.06.2026.

3. Learned counsel for the applicants contended that it was a case of suicide, which resulted from an altercation between the husband and wife. He contended that there was delay of three days in the registration of the FIR. He further contended that the conduct of the complainant and witnesses was unnatural, as [2] no efforts were made to rescue the deceased. He further contended that Mst. Waseeman is the mother of one-and-a-half-year-old son and one daughter aged about three years. Therefore, her incarceration in jail would deprive the children motherhood. He further contended that during the investigation, the prosecution concluded that it was a case of Qatl-bis-Sabab under Section 322 PPC, which, though non-bailable, does not warrant incarceration, as it is only punishable by payment of Diyat. He contended that the case of the applicant party requires further inquiry. He prayed for the grant of bail to the applicants.

4. On the other hand, learned D.P.G for the State opposed the grant of bail on the ground that the applicants are specifically nominated in the FIR and specific roles have been assigned to them. Therefore, they are not entitled to the extraordinary concession of bail. He prayed for the dismissal of the bail application.

5. I have heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned D.P.G. for the State and perused the material available on record. Upon scanning the material available on record, it transpires that the prosecution story was developed that deceased Sajjad was set on fire by Asad and his wife Mst. Waseeman by sprinkling petrol in the presence of witnesses namely, Azhar Salman and Dholan. It transpires from the record that the complainant party were four persons, whereas the accused were only lady Mst. Waseeman and Asad. The conduct of the prosecution witnesses is unnatural, as no efforts were made to rescue Sajjad. Moreover, it was the case of the prosecution that deceased Sajjad was set on fire outside the room. As per the inspection memo, it transpires that the incident took place inside the room. The prosecution witnesses namely Subhan Ali, Maryam, Salman and Dholan, out of whom Salman and Dholan are mentioned in the FIR, as eye witnesses disowned the prosecution story by stating in their statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C that it was a case of suicide which resulted from an exchange of harsh words between the husband and wife.

6. The learned trial Court, while deciding the application in paragraph No. 5, itself observed that it was a case of further inquiry; however, it declined bail on the plea that the incident was grave and gruesome in nature. Whereas, the fact that the incident is grave in nature will not deprive the applicants of the concession of bail, when a case within the scope of section 479(ii) Cr.P.C for further inquiry is made out.

[3] 7. For the foregoing reasons, the case of the applicants requires further inquiry into their guilt. Moreover, Mst. Waseeman is the mother of a suckling child, which also favours her for the grant of bail. Accordingly, the applicants are admitted to post-arrest bail, subject to their furnishing solvent sureties in the sum of Rs.100,000/- (Rupees One Hundred Thousand), each together with personal recognizance bonds in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.

8. Needless to observe that the findings and observations recorded herein are purely tentative in nature and confined to the disposal of the instant bail application. The learned trial Court shall decide the case strictly on the basis of the evidence brought before it, independently and without being influenced by any observation contained in this order.
